name: native-radio-group
description: A set of mutually exclusive options. Controlled only on native — pass value and onValueChange — with each item named by a Label through aria-labelledby.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Callback on value change: (value: string) => void

slots.name: children
slots.description: RadioGroupItem elements, typically paired with Labels

examples.title: Plan picker
examples.description: One row per option, each label wired to its item
examples.code:
<RadioGroup value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>
  {plans.map((option) => (
    <View key={option.id} className="flex-row items-center gap-2">
      <RadioGroupItem value={option.id} aria-labelledby={`plan-${option.id}`} />
      <Label nativeID={`plan-${option.id}`}>{option.label}</Label>
    </View>
  ))}
</RadioGroup>

examples.title: With per-option descriptions
examples.description: Explain each choice under its label
examples.code:
<RadioGroup value={tier} onValueChange={setTier}>
  <View className="flex-row items-start gap-2">
    <RadioGroupItem value="standard" aria-labelledby="tier-standard" className="mt-1" />
    <View className="flex-1">
      <Label nativeID="tier-standard">Standard</Label>
      <Text variant="muted">Delivered in 3-5 days.</Text>
    </View>
  </View>
</RadioGroup>

examples.title: Disabled group
examples.description: Disable every option at the root
examples.code:
<RadioGroup value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan} disabled>
  <View className="flex-row items-center gap-2">
    <RadioGroupItem value="free" aria-labelledby="plan-free" />
    <Label nativeID="plan-free" disabled>Free</Label>
  </View>
</RadioGroup>

ai.whenToUse: Use when the user picks exactly one option from a short visible list — a plan, a shipping speed, a sort order. Keep the value in the parent and give every item its own Label.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for independent on/off choices (use Checkbox per row). Don't use for more than about six options; a Select is easier to scan on a phone. Don't use for an instant-effect setting (use Switch).
commonMistakes: Rendering it uncontrolled — the native primitive needs value and onValueChange, and defaultValue does not exist here, so nothing selects
Omitting aria-labelledby on an item — the dot has no text of its own, so VoiceOver announces an unnamed radio button
Reaching for the orientation prop from the web component — it is web-only; lay the group out with flex classes instead
Removing hitSlop to tighten a row, which drops the 20pt dot well below the 44pt touch minimum
Using a radio group where only one option ever appears, which reads as a control the user cannot act on
ai.accessibilityNotes: Each item is announced as a radio with its checked state, which is what carries the meaning. The root does set role="radiogroup", but React Native does not expose a plain container to assistive tech the way the DOM does, so do not rely on the group itself being announced: precede it with a Label or heading naming the choice. Every item needs its own Label paired by aria-labelledby, and tapping that label selects the option — the practical way to hit a 20pt dot. Disabling at the root disables and dims every item; mirror it on the labels so the whole row reads as unavailable.
